For \(f(k)=m\), we need
\[
\left(m-\frac12\right)^4 \le k < \left(m+\frac12\right)^4.
\]
For \(k\le 1995\), since \(\sqrt[4]{1995}\approx 6.68\), only \(m=1,\dots,7\) occur.

Counts:
\[
\begin{aligned}
m=1 &: k=1,\dots,5 &&\Rightarrow 5\\
m=2 &: k=6,\dots,39 &&\Rightarrow 34\\
m=3 &: k=40,\dots,150 &&\Rightarrow 111\\
m=4 &: k=151,\dots,410 &&\Rightarrow 260\\
m=5 &: k=411,\dots,915 &&\Rightarrow 505\\
m=6 &: k=916,\dots,1785 &&\Rightarrow 870\\
m=7 &: k=1786,\dots,1995 &&\Rightarrow 210
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{1995}\frac1{f(k)}
=5+\frac{34}{2}+\frac{111}{3}+\frac{260}{4}+\frac{505}{5}+\frac{870}{6}+\frac{210}{7}
\]
\[
=5+17+37+65+101+145+30=400.
\]

\[
\boxed{400}
\]
